evidence.method: one-off browser visual inspection plus DOM snapshot; abstract observations only

notes.structure: A wide application shell uses a persistent top bar, a grouped left navigation/filter rail, a dominant central gallery, and a narrower right support rail.
notes.gallery: The central surface is an evenly spaced multi-column shelf of rounded preview panels with compact metadata strips.
notes.pacing: The list is long and regular rather than editorially irregular; repeated card bands create browse-first rhythm.
notes.responsive: The wide shell implies rail collapse and grid reduction on small screens; mobile behavior was not directly captured in this desktop-only observation.

notes.candidate_transfer: The V0 uses open system sans-serif stacks and original labels; it does not retrieve or copy source fonts.

evidence.method: browser visual inspection; font identity not inferred

evidence.method: DOM counts from one browser snapshot; no profiling claim

notes.observed: The page exposes grouped navigation, search/filter controls, theme/preferences controls, and card browsing affordances.
notes.candidate_requirement: V0 must preserve labeled controls, keyboard focus parity, semantic headings, and a reduced-motion alternative; source accessibility is not certified.

evidence.method: accessibility snapshot and candidate policy, not source audit

principles.rule: Use a browse-first gallery when the content is a catalogue: stable card grammar can carry varied previews without making every item a bespoke section.
Keep navigation, browsing, and support content in distinct rails so the central visual field remains the dominant task surface.
Concentrate high-saturation gradients and glow on previews and primary actions instead of flooding the entire shell.
Treat interaction previews as content: one intentional hover/focus transformation should explain why an item is browseable.
When source timing and implementation are unmeasured, preserve the interaction intent with KINETIC tokens and label the result an approximation.

inferences: A distinct generalization target should test repeated component browsing and dark gradient art direction rather than Wanaka's long-form editorial portfolio rhythm.
An original V0 can express the same browse grammar with CSS-generated preview motifs and no source assets, branding, copy, or library code.
The source page's exact responsive and motion behavior remains partially unresolved until human fidelity review.

anti_patterns.issue: Copying source component code, preview media, branding, or exact labels would exceed the abstract-reference policy.
A persistent ambient animation loop would add cost without proving transfer of the browse grammar.
